dial.summary: BTC Accumulation thesis maintained on Sep 2 with 6 of 8 indicators supportive: Global M2 at $103.4T rising on a 4-week basis, real yields at 2.34% and falling (−9bps over 4 weeks), 2s10s steepening to +40bps, Fed balance sheet flat at $6.73T, BTC funding near zero at −0.0048%, and stablecoin dominance declining to 11.28% on a 30-day basis; ISM Manufacturing PMI downshifted to neutral (August 54.6%, below July 55.6%, though expansion continues for the 8th consecutive month); DXY at 99.69 remains in the neutral band; BTC.D at 57.4% holds above the 55% alt-rotation threshold; constructive backdrop ahead of NFP Sep 4, CPI Sep 11, and the pivotal FOMC Sep 16 decision.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; ~6-week reporting lag on full aggregate); US M2 for July 2026 confirmed at $23.22T (29th consecutive monthly increase, +6.11% YoY, record high); global M2 rose ~$0.7T over 4 weeks from ~$102.7T (late June) to $103.4T (July composite); no YoY contraction from any major central bank; August global aggregate not yet available; 4-week uptrend confirmed; status supportive (4-week rising trend met); FOMC Sep 16 is the next key catalyst for global liquidity trajectory.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released Sep 1 at 10:00 AM ET: 54.6%, down 1.0 percentage point from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion); came in below the 55.2% consensus estimate; Production 58.3% (vs July 58.5%), New Orders 53.7% (vs July 56.7%, −3.0pp), Employment 51.2% (vs July 52.8%, −1.6pp); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising, which is not met; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62, neither applies); PMI remains in solid expansion territory corresponding to ~2.4% annualized real GDP growth; S&P Global US Manufacturing PMI final for August at 53.2% (separate survey) also confirms some softening.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.69 on September 2, 2026 (up 0.15% from Sep 1 close of 99.66); 4-week trend down: DXY was approximately 100.3–100.5 in early August 2026 (transitioning from the late July peak of ~100.8–101.0) and has declined to 99.69, a ~−0.8% change over 4 weeks, above the 0.5% flat threshold; status neutral (ICE DXY at 99.69 within 97.5–100 neutral band); structural dollar weakness driven by Treasury buyback program and rate-cut expectations ahead of FOMC Sep 16; NFP Sep 4 and CPI Sep 11 are the next decisive inputs—a dovish macro outcome cluster would accelerate DXY toward or below 97.5 (supportive territory).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 at 2.34% as of August 27, 2026 (most recent available; FRED proxy-blocked this run); cross-check: Aug 20 reading confirmed at 2.35% per MacroRadar, consistent with 2.34% Aug 27 FRED print; 4-week trend down: ~2.43% (July 25, 2026) → 2.34% (Aug 27) = −9bps, a confirmed falling trend; 10Y nominal yield at 4.80% on Sep 1 (up 4bps); status supportive (falling 4-week trend satisfies supportive condition per rule); headwind rule requires both rising AND above 2%—the above-2% criterion is met, but the falling trend dominates status scoring; CPI Sep 11 and FOMC Sep 16 are the next compression catalysts.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 2, 2026 estimate: 10Y yield 4.80% (Sep 1, up 4bps); 2Y yield 4.40% (Sep 1); implied spread +40bps (+0.40%); 4-week steepening trend intact: ~+35bps (early August 2026) → +40bps (Sep 2 estimate) = +5bps steepening over 4 weeks; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening direction intact); upcoming catalysts: NFP (Sep 4), ECB (Sep 10), CPI (Sep 11), and FOMC (Sep 16) are the next curve-shaping inputs.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: ~$6.73T for week ending August 27, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 27); next H.4.1 release scheduled September 3, 2026—no new WALCL data available this run (FRED proxy-blocked); 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (late July / early August) → $6.73T (Aug 27) = ~+$31B (+0.5%), within the flat threshold; routine measured QT operations continue at a steady pace; no aggressive QT signal and no overnight rate spike; status supportive (holding flat at post-2022 stabilization plateau; QT pace stable).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately −0.0048% (CoinGlass proxy-blocked; value held from prior verified MacroMicro aggregate observation); search data confirms funding near zero and slightly negative in late August / early September 2026, consistent with spot-driven price action and no levered long overextension; BTC.D at 57.4% on Sep 2 (above 55% alt-rotation threshold); Bitcoin price ~$77,600 (Sep 2, 2026); total crypto market cap ~$2.7T; 30-day trend flat: near zero throughout August; well below the +0.04%/8h overheating headwind threshold; status supportive (near-zero funding, no long-side overextension signal).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$305B (Sep 2, 2026); total crypto market cap $2.7T (CoinGecko, Sep 2 at 1:30 AM UTC, down 1.4% in 24h); stablecoin dominance 11.28% (305/2700); BTC.D 57.4% (Sep 2, above 55% alt-rotation threshold); Bitcoin price ~$77,600; 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% in early August 2026 to 11.28% today; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition—dominance rising while TOTAL also rises—does not apply as total crypto market cap declined in 24h); BTC.D holding above 55% keeps Alt Rotation signal un-triggered.

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases the August 2026 Non-Manufacturing PMI at 10:00 AM ET—services sector counterpart to manufacturing ISM (August Manufacturing: 54.6%, neutral); services represent ~80% of US GDP; released one business day ahead of the August NFP report (September 4); a sustained services expansion above 55 reinforces the soft-landing narrative; a sub-50 reading alongside the softening manufacturing ISM would materially shift FOMC odds toward a 50bps cut on Sep 16.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 29, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 29—released same day as ISM Services PMI; provides additional framing ahead of the August NFP report (September 4) and FOMC September 16; a spike above 220K reinforces the case for an aggressive cut; a stable-to-declining read keeps the policy debate open heading into NFP.

upcoming.title: Nonfarm Payrolls (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—second-to-last major data point before FOMC September 16 (after CPI Sep 11); July 2026 NFP shocked at −23K (vs +79K forecast), ADP July +44K; a further contraction would strongly argue for a 50bps rate cut and push DXY toward or below 97.5 (supportive for risk assets); a rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative; also includes unemployment rate, average hourly earnings, and labor force participation rate.
